chunks: Al-Bazofari from Humayd ibn al-Ziyad from al-Hasan from Muhammad ibn al-Ziyad from 'Ammar ibn Marwan from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I said to him: 'A man has a female slave and her daughter, and he has sexual relations with one of them, causing her to die, while the other remains. Is it permissible for him to have sexual relations with the other?' He said, 'No.'

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id said: 'I wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): A man had a female slave whom he used sexually, and she died or he sold her. Then later he had relations with her mother. Is it permissible for him to marry her? He wrote back (peace be upon him): 'It is not permissible for him.'
ai.seo_question: Can a man marry the mother of his female slave if he had relations with her?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the distinction between *al-bina'* (concubinage) and *al-nikah* (marriage) as the legal causes for prohibiting marriage to the mother. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes that sexual relations with a slave girl create a permanent prohibition on her mother, regardless of whether the girl dies or is sold, unless the man formally marries the slave girl, which severs the specific bond of concubinage. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that the prohibition stems from the act of possession through concubinage rather than a formal marital contract.
